text:
incident-bot: P0 pager triggered: multiple TP4 training jobs failing with NCCL timeouts and CUDA Xid 79 on several nodes. Automatic oncall notify sent.

sophie: I'm oncall for the next 6h, taking this. first pass: which clusters/nodes?

mike: hitting it on gpu-07, gpu-09, gpu-11 in us-west. All are running the TP4 swarm autoscaler jobs. Error in trainer logs: 'Unrecoverable NCCL ERROR: Unhandled system error' then processes spin, kv cache grows, OOM on one replica.

anya: saw similar on test-train-az. Kernel logs show repeated Xid 79 around the same timestamps. dmesg snippet: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=4210, GPU=0: PTE corruption or a memory access fault
[ 1234.567891] gpu-collector: process 4210 (trainer) killed by signal 6
```

elaine: customer-facing impact: two customers running high-throughput inference pipelines saw 503s and increased latency starting ~09:12 UTC. CS ticket #4281, reporting ~12% error rate for affected routes.

sophie: thanks. prioritized mitigation to reduce blast radius: 1) identify bad nodes and cordon/drain, 2) fallback model routing to single-GPU model variant, 3) set NCCL env tweaks as short-term stopgap, 4) avoid full fleet restarts.

infra-bot: Node list with crash counts in last 15m: gpu-07(6), gpu-09(5), gpu-11(8), gpu-03(1).

shane: I'm on infra; recommend cordon gpu-11 and move running pods. Running drain now: `kubectl drain gpu-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

mike: logs from trainer (trimmed): 
```
2026-03-15T09:11:58Z WARN nccl: aborting communicator 0x7f2c... status 14 (timeout)
2026-03-15T09:12:01Z ERROR runtime: kv cache size 1.2GB, attempting eviction
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z FATAL cuda: driver error: Xid 79
```

anya: quick config tweak proposal: set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 and NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 on affected jobs to prefer system sockets instead of IB. Also try NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS. This has reduced failures in earlier runs.

sophie: agree. but IB disable might increase latency; do for small subset. We'll apply to the canary pool first. Can someone patch the job spec with env override?

devops: I'll patch the canary namespace jobs with: 
```yaml
env:
  - name: NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME
    value: eth0
  - name: NCCL_IB_DISABLE
    value: "1"
  - name: NCCL_P2P_LEVEL
    value: SYS
```
Applying now to canary-ml-1.

support-bot: Customer impact summary: 2 premium customers, ~8 inference endpoints degraded, average latency spike +450ms, errors 12-15% between 09:11-09:24 UTC. No data exfiltration.

elaine: CS is drafting a short update to customers: root cause under investigation, mitigation in progress, ETA for stable routing ~30-60m.

infra-bot: Drain of gpu-11 finished. Evict success: 18 pods moved to healthy nodes. Node marked scheduling-disabled.

mike: after moving workloads off gpu-11, one of the jobs recovered a bit but still seeing intermittent NCCL timeouts on gpu-09. Could be a fabric/driver mismatch on some nodes. Driver version: 535.86 on gpu-09, 535.86 on gpu-11, but gpu-07 shows 535.84 (older).

sophie: driver mismatch is a likely vector. For now: 1) cordon nodes with older drivers (gpu-07), 2) schedule a rolling driver sync in maintenance window, 3) keep canary patched with NCCL env. Anyone have a safe script to restart only trainer containers (avoid model servers)?

shane: use this in node agent to restart training pods by label: 
```bash
kubectl get pods -l workload=trainer -o name --field-selector=status.phase=Running | xargs -r -n1 kubectl delete pod --grace-period=30
```
We'll run that on nodes after cordon to let scheduler place pods on healthy nodes.

mike: also enabling extra NCCL debug logs to confirm whether the errors are link-level or memory corruption: set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO on canary.

anya: note: if Xid 79 persists after driver sync, could be hardware flakiness. Recommend running `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` and `nvidia-healthmon` diagnostics on affected GPUs.

sophie: action items (live):
- shane: cordon gpu-07, gpu-09 (in progress) and run `nvidia-smi` diagnostics.
- devops: patch canary jobs with NCCL env overrides (done).
- mike: monitor canary and collect nccl debug logs.
- elaine: customer update drafted and sent at 09:30 UTC.
- anya: prepare playbook for driver rolling upgrade.

devops: canary patch applied and canary throughput looks stable for 5m. No new NCCL timeouts in canary pool since env changes.

infra-bot: Cordon gpu-07 complete. Diagnostics show ECC errors on gpu-07: `ECC errors: 34 correctable, 2 uncorrectable` — raising hardware flag.

mike: uncorrectable ECC errors -> escalate hardware. We should isolate gpu-07 permanently and kick off RMA for that board.

sophie: good catch. escalate to hw replacement queue and mark node for rebuild. I'll file an ops ticket. In the short term, continue to route sensitive latency customers off affected AZ.

support-bot: CS sent an update to affected customers at 09:32 UTC: we're mitigating and routing traffic; next update in 60 minutes or sooner.

anya: follow-up note: for TP jobs, it's safer to have explicit communicator timeouts lower than default to surface issues earlier and fall back to compatible single-GPU variant automatically. Suggest adding a fallback policy to rollout config.

sophie: agreed. add fallback to routing policy: if more than 5% error rate for 2 consecutive minutes, route to single-GPU variant. devops, can you add that to the gate config?

devops: adding route fallback rule now to gateway config. Pushing in 2m.

mike: monitoring: overall cluster NCCL timeout rate trending down after canary env change and cordons. Error spikes reduced from ~120/min to ~8/min across fleet.

sophie: closing loop: immediate mitigations worked. Long-term items: driver version enforcement at provisioning, expand GPU health checks (ECC thresholds), automated fallback routing for TP jobs, and a playbook for Xid 79 (hardware vs driver triage). Filing follow-ups with owners.

elaine: thanks team. I'll coordinate postmortem and customer follow-ups once we have RCA.

incident-bot: Incident escalated -> postmortem required. Severity: P0 -> severity review scheduled. (reaction :rotating_light:)

sophie: thanks everyone. staying on for the handoff to the night on-call at 10:00 UTC. if anything spikes, ping me.
